Debt = short-term borrowings 83,587.4 + non-current liabilities due within one year 3,803.3 + long-term borrowings 14,789.2 + bonds 3,000.0 + lease liabilities 25.2 + other current liabilities 6,183.5 and other non-current liabilities 115.6 (these map to IFRS 'Deposits from related parties' -- JCC Finance's deposit book, debt-like; Dec-25 IFRS 5,592 vs PRC 5,918). Cash-like assets (all interest/return-bearing, because interest income is stripped from the flows) = cash and bank 54,760.0 (incl. restricted futures-margin/bill-pledge deposits) + held-for-trading financial assets 10,673.8 + non-current assets due within one year 1,815.3 (time deposits) + other debt investment 660.8 + other non-current financial assets 947.9 + other equity instruments 59.3 + non-current time/restricted deposits and loans to related parties 2,509.4 (Dec-25 IFRS values, sitting inside 'other non-current assets') + current loans to related parties 2,601.4 (Dec-25 IFRS value, inside other receivables). Derivatives are treated as part of hedged inventory working capital (not bridged): derivative liabilities fell 7,673 -> 338 in Q1 as hedges settled.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment expense in FY2018-FY2025 annual reports (SBC-zero PRC SOE); EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year. SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buybacks nil; FY2024 RMB258.7m (one-off H-share repurchase). Flat count is a convention the company does not need to fund since SBC is nil.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in RMB (CNY); H-share quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1721 HKD per CNY, Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-10T03:38Z. Parity check against the A-share line (600362.SS, 2026-10-09 close, CNY 42.51 = HKD 49.83 at this rate): the H-share at current_price trades roughly a third below the A-share (A/H premium ~50%), the usual SOE dual-listing gap -- no exact parity exists, but the direction of the rate is confirmed (H price / 1.1721 lands below the CNY A-share price, as expected). Per-share values are computed in CNY and converted at this rate; refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular close (HKEX), Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. Rf 1.9% (10y China Government Bond, 2026); ERP 6.5% (China); levered beta ~1.25 for a smelting/trading copper cyclical with ~45-50% gearing -> cost of equity ~10.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~3.1% (FY2025 interest paid 2,325 / ~75bn average borrowings) -> 2.3% after 25% tax. Target weights ~80% equity / 20% debt (market cap ~98bn CNY at the H price vs ~37bn net debt). WACC = 0.8 x 10.0 + 0.2 x 2.3 = 8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: copper-cycle risk is charged in the scenario flows, not stacked in the discount rate (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities (25.2m at 31-Mar-26; 224m at Dec-25) are in total_debt; lease principal (192m FY2025) is NOT deducted from the flows; right-of-use additions (~117m/yr) are inside the capex % path. Immaterial at this scale (<0.05% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once, in the bridge: consolidated flows (NCI share of FY2025 profit 361m, ~4.7%) and NCI book value 13,434.8m at 31-Mar-26 deducted in equity_bridge. Capitalised NCI earnings (~4bn at 9%) would be lower; book is used as the more conservative claim and because FY2025's 3.0bn NCI contributions are not yet earning.
inputs.fy0_calibration: FY2025 operating EBITDA ex non-operating items = reported EBITDA 16,295 (operating income 12,897 incl. all other income/gains + D&A 3,398) - interest income 1,914 - dividend income 18 - share of associates/JVs 222 - BOCI reclassification/associate disposal gain 1,148 + non-cash PPE/other asset impairments 1,160 = 14,154 (2.61% of revenue). Modelled FY0 NOPAT (14,154 - 3,398) x 0.75 = 8,067 vs reported profit incl NCI 7,734 + after-tax net finance cost 421 - associates 222 = 7,933: ties within 2%. Same normalisation gives 2.21-2.64% for FY2018-FY2024 (avg ~2.47%).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (CNY flows / HKD quote, SBC-zero, NCI, associates at fair value, matching-asset rule) and MID-CYCLE normalisation. Routing: Jiangxi Copper is an integrated copper smelter/miner with a large trading arm and a captive finance company -- an operating company, not a bank/holdco, so owner-FCF applies; JCC Finance's deposit book is treated as debt and its loans/deposits as cash-like. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). MID-CYCLE: copper is at a record (COMEX HG=F US$6.69/lb, ~US$14,750/t, 52-week range 4.90-6.83) and H1 FY2026 attributable profit was RMB8.63bn (+107% YoY, partly derivative fair-value gains) vs FY2025 RMB7.37bn. Reported FY2025 FCF (-11.4bn, a 19.2bn inventory build) and cumulative FY2018-25 owner FCF (-1.4bn) are not a base; instead FY2026 (mostly realised) is modelled as an elevated year at 3.6% operating EBITDA margin, FY2027 as a price normalisation (revenue -10%, working capital released), and FY2028+ at a mid-cycle 2.6% margin -- the FY2018-25 normalised average (2.47%) plus a modest uplift for the shift away from low-margin trading (trading share 49% -> 27% of revenue). Revenue after FY2027 sits at roughly FY2025 levels (avg LME ~US$9.9k/t) compounding at 2.5-3% nominal. Working capital is the main cash sink: wc_capture -9% of the revenue CHANGE (NWC/revenue 8.6% FY2024, 11.5% FY2025), so price rises consume cash and price falls release it. SolGold (Cascabel, Ecuador; scheme effective 4-Mar-2026, net cash paid 6,869m in Q1) is valued at its deal equity value in the bridge and its development capex is EXCLUDED from the flows (assumed NPV-neutral); FY2026 'investment plan' of RMB26.6bn includes this equity spend. FQM 18.47% stake (equity-accounted, share of profit stripped from flows) bridged at market value. H1 FY2026 interim report (Aug 2026) is not in Extracted/, so the Q1 FY2026 balance sheet is the latest anchor; H1 figures used qualitatively only.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: equity 5yr CAGR 6.29% and revenue 5yr 11.3% both embed the FY2020->FY2025 copper upcycle (FY2020 trough base); post-normalisation growth of 2.5-3% nominal (volume ~1-2% + price inflation) used instead
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR 27.3% vs equity 5yr CAGR 6.3% (and revenue 11.3%): >30% divergence. EPS growth is measured from the FY2020 trough (0.64) and reflects the copper price cycle, not compounding; equity growth was further held down by dividends and FQM OCI swings.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - interest income; SBC nil) FY2018-FY2025: 5,048 / 3,996 / -3,061 / 5,464 / 4,240 / 2,328 / -6,123 / -13,295 -- cumulative -1.4bn over eight years while equity rose 49.8 -> 81.3bn. FCF CAGRs are not meaningful (negative endpoints). Reported profit growth in rising-price years is consumed by working capital (inventory, futures margin, prepayments); the model reflects that through a negative wc_capture rather than by ignoring it.

base.narrative: FY2026 realised high (H1 revenue +19.5%), then copper reverts toward ~US$10-11k/t and revenue returns to ~FY2025 levels by FY2028; operating EBITDA margin settles at 2.6% (normalised FY2018-25 average 2.47% + trading mix shift); TC/RCs stay thin but by-product gold/silver/acid carry the smelters; capex ~1% of revenue (ex-Cascabel).

bull.narrative: Structural copper deficit holds prices well above the last cycle (~US$12-13k/t); TC/RCs recover as Chinese smelter capacity is rationalised; mix shift from trading to processing materials (copper foil, PV ribbon) lifts the through-cycle margin to 3.0%.

bear.narrative: Copper falls back to ~US$9k/t as China property and macro weakness meet new mine supply; TC/RCs stay at or below zero so purchased-concentrate smelting (~78% of feed) earns little; H1-2026 derivative gains prove non-recurring; margin reverts to the low end of the FY2018-25 range (2.1%).

scenario_narratives.base: Jiangxi Copper earns a through-cycle 2.6% operating EBITDA margin on a revenue base that is mostly a copper-price pass-through. FY2026 is booked as an elevated year (record copper, gold and silver; H1 attributable profit RMB8.63bn), then prices normalise and the working capital the upcycle absorbed is partly released. Thin smelting economics (zero 2026 TC benchmark) are offset by by-products and own-mine output (~200kt concentrate). Value rests as much on the balance sheet -- the FQM stake at market, SolGold, JCC Finance's liquid assets -- as on the operating flows, whose FCF conversion has historically been poor.
scenario_narratives.bull: The structural-deficit thesis plays out: grid, EV and AI data-centre demand keeps copper near US$12-13k/t, Chinese smelter rationalisation restores positive treatment charges, and the deliberate shift from trading into processing materials lifts the through-cycle margin to ~3%. FQM and SolGold give reserve growth without full greenfield spending.
scenario_narratives.bear: Copper reverts to ~US$9k/t, treatment charges stay negative for a smelter that buys ~78% of its concentrate, and the FY2025-H1 2026 profit surge proves to be price and derivative effects. Margins revert to ~2.1%, working capital stays heavy, and SOE/dual-listing governance (H-share discount, capped FQM stake, overseas approvals) keeps the H-share at a deep discount to book.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default because copper is at a record and the valuation date sits at a probable cyclical peak, earnings quality is mixed (H1-2026 derivative gains, eight years of near-zero cumulative owner FCF), and smelting margins depend on treatment charges currently below zero. Bull cut to 25% because it needs both sustained high copper prices and a TC recovery. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF for a commodity price-taker: do not capitalise record copper prices or a single year's FCF (FY2025: -11.4bn). Flows are operating only (interest income, associates and one-offs stripped); every stripped stream has its asset in the bridge -- JCC Finance's deposits and investments as cash-like, FQM at market, SolGold at deal value. Cyclical terminal cap of 12x FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Copper price: the base assumes reversion from ~US$14.75k/t to ~US$10-11k/t; a structurally higher price (bull) is worth materially more.
Working capital: wc_capture -9% of revenue change; the FY2025 build (19.2bn inventory) shows how large swings are, and the sign flips value between years.
FQM stake marked at market (~28bn CNY, ~30% of the H-share market cap): a 30% move in FQM is ~RMB2.5/share.
Treatment/refining charges at zero or negative for a smelter that buys most of its feed.
SolGold/Cascabel development capex excluded from flows on an NPV-neutral assumption.
H1 FY2026 interim balance sheet not extracted; anchors are 31-Mar-2026.
